trust_decision.summary: The gateway must only read objects from the object store fixed by its own `[object_storage]` config; at the pinned commit it instead rebuilds a store from a caller-supplied `StoragePath.kind` (filesystem root, or bucket/region/endpoint/allow_http), so a caller picks the filesystem root that is read and the S3 endpoint the gateway dials with its own credentials.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the internal object storage endpoint; the handler is the first thing an engineer opens, and it deserializes the whole caller-supplied `StoragePath` and passes it straight to the fetch.

fix_sites.entry_point: `Client::get_object` public Rust SDK method (embedded mode calls the sink at :1336, HTTP mode calls the endpoint at :1330)
UI server client `TensorZeroClient.getObject` (serializes the whole StoragePath into `?storage_path=`)
UI server-side renderer resolving files of datapoints/inferences for display

O3_reason_to_dismiss: `StoragePath` is documented as public API for `File`s (crates/tensorzero-types/src/storage.rs:44-46) and the hardened code's own doc comment declares `get_object` a trusted entry point that in-process callers such as the evaluations crate may use, so a solver can call these routes intended design rather than a gap.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Resolving a `StoragePath` whose `kind` was recorded under a different `[object_storage]` configuration than the one currently loaded: the datapoint/stored-inference roundtrip and the UI keep the recorded `kind`, and the published fix had to re-point every e2e config glob at a matching S3 bucket (`fix.diff:151-163`, `fix.diff:93-113`) for those flows to keep working. A blanket refusal to honour the recorded kind breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: `storage_path` as a JSON-encoded `StoragePath` in the query string (old shape) versus a plain object key in `path` (new shape)
path strings carrying `..`, `.`, duplicated or empty segments
absolute-looking path such as `/etc/passwd` (normalized under the prefix, not the host root)
`kind.type = filesystem` with a caller-chosen root directory
`kind.type = s3_compatible` with caller-chosen bucket_name, region, endpoint and allow_http
`kind.type = disabled`, and no `[object_storage]` configured at all
UI side: full `ZodStoragePath` object versus bare string

O7_producer.where: crates/tensorzero-types/src/storage.rs:21-60 (StorageKind/StoragePath serde schema), persisted verbatim into datapoint and inference rows at crates/tensorzero-core/src/inference/types/mod.rs:628-638

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /inference (and /batch_inference) with a `file` of `file_type: object_storage_pointer` whose `storage_path.kind` names a filesystem root or an S3 endpoint; the lazy file future fetches through the same sink
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: `StoragePath` is documented public API for `File`s, so 'clients reference files in their own bucket' looks like intended behaviour, and the fix left this module untouched.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same crate, different module (inference/types vs endpoints); the request path enters through endpoints/inference.rs, ~500 lines from the handler file

O8_uncovered_routes.route: One request persists a caller-chosen `StoragePath.kind` into a datapoint or stored inference, and a later read re-resolves it through `StoragePathResolver::resolve` for `Config`
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The stored `kind` was written by the gateway itself, so it reads as trusted roundtrip state rather than caller input.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: three files apart across inference-types and dataset conversion code; the write side is in endpoints/datasets/v1/conversion_utils.rs

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A write-side twin of the fetch that selects a store from a supplied `StoragePath.kind` instead of the configured store.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already receives both `&Option<ObjectStoreInfo>` and a `StoragePath`, and using only the configured store is the single difference from the read path; a maintainer adding 'upload into the user's own bucket' would copy `get_object`'s Cow match.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second fetch helper for another transport (e.g. a GCS or plain-HTTP object fetch) that keeps taking a `StoragePath` while the JSON endpoint takes a bare key.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The store-selection match lives here already, and the fix's own doc comment carves out a 'trusted in-process' variant, which invites another caller-shaped entry point beside it.

O9_family: arbitrary file read and SSRF through caller-controlled object-store selection (CWE-552 / CWE-918)

O10_build.language: Rust (workspace) plus TypeScript for the ui/ package
O10_build.toolchain: cargo; workspace MSRV bumped to 1.94.0 in a recent commit; crates/.cargo/config.toml defines the e2e build aliases
services: none for the object-storage unit tests (TempDir + LocalFileSystem)
ClickHouse, Postgres, Valkey and S3/MinIO for the full e2e suites
O10_build.project_tests: crates/tensorzero-core/tests/e2e/object_storage.rs (HTTP e2e against the running gateway), crates/tensorzero-core/tests/e2e/providers/common.rs:1421-1470 (`check_object_fetch`, embedded handler), and the new inline `#[cfg(test)]` tests the fix adds around the filesystem store; unit runs use `cargo test -p tensorzero-core`.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep accepting the JSON `StoragePath` and add `..`/prefix checks on `storage_path.path` (the path component was already `Path::parse`d at crates/tensorzero-types/src/storage.rs:84-89), leaving the caller-supplied `kind` to build the store.
